cemc-fermat-2006-06.title: Add the discounts
cemc-fermat-2006-06.body:
T-shirt: $0.3\times25=7.50$ dollars. Jeans: $0.1\times75=7.50$ dollars. Total: 15 dollars.

**Answer: (A) \$15**

cemc-fermat-2006-07.title: Even exponents
cemc-fermat-2006-07.body:
$2^3\cdot5\cdot p$ must be a perfect square, so every prime must appear an even number of times. $p$ needs at least one more 2 and one more 5: $p=10$, giving $2^4\cdot5^2=400=20^2$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

cemc-fermat-2006-09.title: Exterior angle
cemc-fermat-2006-09.body:
$F$ lies on $CA$ extended, so $\angle FAB=70^\circ$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$ and equals $\angle ABC+\angle ACB=(20+x)+(x+20)$.

$70=2x+40$, so $x=15$.

**Answer: (A) 15**

cemc-fermat-2006-10.title: Count side by side
cemc-fermat-2006-10.body:
A straight segment meets the boundary of a rectangle (a convex shape) in at most 2 points (unless it overlaps a side, which gives infinitely many). Each of the 4 sides of one rectangle therefore meets the other rectangle at most twice: at most $4\times2=8$ points.

8 is achievable: place two congruent squares with the same centre, one rotated $45^\circ$ — each side of one cuts two sides of the other, forming an 8-pointed star outline.

**Answer: (D) 8**

cemc-fermat-2006-15.title: Perpendicular bisector
cemc-fermat-2006-15.body:
The fold is the perpendicular bisector of the segment. Its midpoint is $(3,1)$, and the segment has slope $\frac{3-(-1)}{5-1}=1$, so the fold has slope $-1$: $y-1=-(x-3)$, i.e. $y=-x+4$.

**Answer: (D) $y=-x+4$**

cemc-fermat-2006-15.title: Equal distances
cemc-fermat-2006-15.body:
Points on the fold are equally far from both points: $(x-5)^2+(y-3)^2=(x-1)^2+(y+1)^2$. Expanding, $-10x-6y+34=-2x+2y+2$, so $8x+8y=32$, i.e. $y=-x+4$.

**Answer: (D) $y=-x+4$**

cemc-fermat-2006-16.title: Half the rectangle
cemc-fermat-2006-16.body:
Circle + shaded region = the whole rectangle, area $8\cdot9=72$. Equal areas means the circle has area 36: $\pi r^2=36$, so $r=\sqrt{\frac{36}{\pi}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt\pi}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{6}{\sqrt\pi}$**

cemc-fermat-2006-17.title: Use the rule term by term
cemc-fermat-2006-17.body:
Fourth term: $5+p+q=13$, so $p+q=8$. Fifth term: $r=p+q+13=21$. Seventh term: $x=13+r+40=74$. (Check: sixth term $q+13+21=40$ gives $q=6$, $p=2$.)

**Answer: (D) 74**

cemc-fermat-2006-18.title: Distance over circumference
cemc-fermat-2006-18.body:
6 minutes is $\frac1{10}$ h, so she rode $2.4$ km $=2400$ m. One rotation covers $0.75\pi\approx2.356$ m. Rotations: $\frac{2400}{0.75\pi}=\frac{3200}{\pi}\approx1018.6$, closest to **1020**.

**Answer: (B) 1020**

cemc-fermat-2006-19.title: Break into pieces
cemc-fermat-2006-19.body:
Let $[ABC]=x$.

- $\triangle ADE\cong\triangle ABC$ (two sides equal and vertical angles at $A$), so its area is $x$. Likewise $\triangle BGF$ and $\triangle CKH$ have area $x$.
- $\triangle CFE$ has $CE=2CA$, $CF=2CB$ and shares angle $C$, so it is similar to $\triangle CBA$ with ratio 2 and area $4x$. Hence quadrilateral $AEFB$ has area $3x$. Similarly $ADKC$ and $BCHG$ each have area $3x$.

Hexagon: $x+3x+3\cdot3x=13x$. Ratio **13 : 1**.

**Answer: (E) 13 : 1**

cemc-fermat-2006-21.title: Odd versus even $n$
cemc-fermat-2006-21.body:
**$n$ odd:** $n-1$ and $n+1$ are consecutive even numbers, one a multiple of 4, so their product has at least three factors of 2. All 39 odd $n$ from 3 to 79 work.

**$n$ even:** $n-1$ and $n+1$ are odd, so all factors of 2 come from $n$: we need $8\mid n$. That gives $8,16,\dots,80$: 10 values.

Total: $39+10=49$.

**Answer: (E) 49**

cemc-fermat-2006-23.title: Cosine law
cemc-fermat-2006-23.body:
Let the time be $t$. Then $TC=5t$, $JC=3t$ and $TJ=15$. Since $JE=EH=15$, $\angle HJE=45^\circ$, so $\angle TJC=135^\circ$.

$$25t^2=225+9t^2-2(15)(3t)\cos135^\circ=225+9t^2+45\sqrt2\,t,$$
so $16t^2-45\sqrt2\,t-225=0$ and
$$t=\frac{45\sqrt2+\sqrt{4050+14400}}{32}\approx\frac{63.64+135.83}{32}\approx6.23.$$
Closest to **6.2** s.

**Answer: (E) 6.2**

cemc-fermat-2006-23.title: Coordinates
cemc-fermat-2006-23.body:
Put $T=(0,0)$, $E=(30,0)$, $H=(30,15)$, $J=(15,0)$. Jerry moves along direction $(1,1)/\sqrt2$, so after $t$ s he is at $\left(15+\frac{3t}{\sqrt2},\frac{3t}{\sqrt2}\right)$.

Tom's distance: $\left(15+\frac{3t}{\sqrt2}\right)^2+\frac{9t^2}{2}=25t^2$, which simplifies to the same equation $16t^2-45\sqrt2\,t-225=0$, so $t\approx6.23$ s.

**Answer: (E) 6.2**

cemc-fermat-2006-24.title: Divisibility
cemc-fermat-2006-24.body:
The left side is $\frac{11}{6a}$, so $6a=11(b^2-2b)$. Then $11\mid a$; write $a=11A$, giving $b^2-2b=6A$, i.e. $6\mid b(b-2)$, with $b\ge3$.

$b=3,4,5$ give $3,8,15$ — not multiples of 6. $b=6$ gives $24$, so $A=4$, $a=44$. Since $a$ grows with $b$, this is the minimum: $a+b=50$.

**Answer: (E) 50**

cemc-fermat-2006-25.title: Cross-section through one cone's axis
cemc-fermat-2006-25.body:
The base centres form an equilateral triangle of side 100, so the sphere's centre lies above its centroid, at horizontal distance $\frac{100}{\sqrt3}$ from each cone's axis.

Take the vertical cross-section through one cone's axis and the sphere's centre $O$. In it, the cone's slant edge goes from the apex $X$ (height 120, horizontal position 0) down to the base rim $Y$ (height 0, horizontal position 50), with length $\sqrt{50^2+120^2}=130$. The sphere appears as a circle of radius $r$ touching this edge at $P$ and touching the top level at $H$, with $XH=\frac{100}{\sqrt3}$.

Tangents from $X$: $XP=XH=\frac{100}{\sqrt3}$, so $PY=130-\frac{100}{\sqrt3}$.

Let $G$ be the point at height 0 below $O$; then $OG=120-r$ and $GY=\frac{100}{\sqrt3}-50$. Computing $OY^2$ two ways:
$$r^2+\left(130-\tfrac{100}{\sqrt3}\right)^2=\left(\tfrac{100}{\sqrt3}-50\right)^2+(120-r)^2.$$
Using $130^2=50^2+120^2$, this simplifies to $240r=\frac{2\cdot80\cdot100}{\sqrt3}$, so $r=\frac{200}{3\sqrt3}=\frac{200\sqrt3}{9}\approx38.49$. Closest to **38.5**.

**Answer: (D) 38.5**

cemc-fermat-2006-25.title: Half-angle at the apex
cemc-fermat-2006-25.body:
In the same cross-section, both the top level $XH$ and the slant edge $XY$ leave the apex $X$ towards the sphere, and the circle touches both, so $XO$ bisects $\angle HXY$.

$\angle HXY=\theta$ is the angle of the slant edge below the horizontal: $\tan\theta=\frac{120}{50}$, so $\sin\theta=\frac{12}{13}$ and $\cos\theta=\frac{5}{13}$. Then
$$\tan\angle OXH=\tan\tfrac\theta2=\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}=\frac{12/13}{18/13}=\frac23.$$
In right $\triangle OHX$: $r=OH=XH\cdot\frac23=\frac{100}{\sqrt3}\cdot\frac23=\frac{200}{3\sqrt3}\approx38.49$.

**Answer: (D) 38.5**
